48:1: It means by the Almighty’s saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, meaning: Indeed, We have decreed for you, O Muhammad, a judgment for whoever hears it or hears it, over those of the disbelievers of your people who oppose you and are hostile to you, and We have decreed for you victory and triumph over them, so that you may thank your Lord and praise Him for His blessing in His decreeing for you over them and His granting you what He granted you, and that you may glorify Him and seek His forgiveness, so that your Lord may forgive you for your deeds, whatever sin you committed before He granted you what He granted you, and whatever sins you committed after He granted you what He granted you. That is what you thanked Him for and sought His forgiveness. We have chosen this statement in interpreting this verse because of the evidence of the statement of God, the Exalted, the Majestic, {When there comes the help of God and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of God in multitudes, then exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance}, as God, the Exalted, commanded him to exalt with praise of his Lord when God’s help and the conquest of Mecca came to him, and to ask His forgiveness, and informed him that He is the Accepter of repentance for whoever does that. In that is a clear statement that the statement of God, the Exalted, the Majestic, {So that God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come} is only information from God, the Exalted, to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about His reward for his thanks to Him, for the blessing that He bestowed upon him by revealing to him what He conquered, because God, the Exalted, rewards His servants for their deeds and nothing else. And after that, in the authenticity of the report about him, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he would stand until his feet swelled, so it was said to him: O Messenger of God, do you do this while your past and future sins have been forgiven? He said: Should I not be a grateful servant?” This is clear evidence that what we have said is the correct statement, and that God, the Blessed and Exalted, only promised His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgiveness for his past sins, the opening that He opened for him, and the coming ones, based on his gratitude to Him, for the blessings that He bestowed upon him. Likewise, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would say: I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him for every hundred times. If the statement in this regard was that God the Most High informed His Prophet that He had forgiven him for his past and future sins in a manner other than the one we have mentioned, then His command to him to seek forgiveness after this verse, and the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) seeking forgiveness from his Lord for his sins after it, would not have had a rational meaning. For seeking forgiveness means: the servant asking his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, to forgive his sins. So if there are no sins that can be forgiven, then his asking Him to forgive them would have no meaning, because it is impossible for him to say: O God, forgive me for a sin that I did not commit. Some of them interpreted this to mean: So that He may forgive you for your past sins before the message, and for those that came after until the time when He said: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest * That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come. As for the conquest that God Almighty promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, this number in gratitude to him for it, it is what was mentioned in the truce that took place between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists of Quraysh at Al-Hudaybiyah. It was mentioned that this Surah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon his return from Al-Hudaybiyah after the truce that took place between him and his people. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. Conquest means judgment. Mention the narration of the one who said that this Surah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the time mentioned. Humaid bin Masada told us: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Amer: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. He said: Al-Hudaybiyyah. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, he said: He slaughtered him at Al-Hudaibiyah and shaved his head. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay` narrated: Abu Bahr narrated: Shu`bah narrated: Jami` ibn Shaddad narrated: `Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi `Ulqamah said: I heard `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud say: “When we returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah, we camped and slept, and we did not wake up until the sun had risen. We woke up and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asleep. We said: ‘Wake him up.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) woke up and said: ‘Do as you used to do, for the same applies to one who sleeps or forgets.’ We missed the she-camel of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and found its halter caught in a tree. I brought it to him and he mounted it. While we were traveling, the revelation came to him. When it came to him, he would be distressed, but when he recovered, he informed us that the following had been revealed to him: ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest.’” Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam narrated to us: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Anas ibn Malik who said: “When we returned from the Battle of Hudaybiyyah, we were prevented from performing our rituals. We were in a state of sadness and depression. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path,’ or as God willed. Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A verse has been revealed to me that is more beloved to me than the entire world.’” Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Urooba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, regarding the verse, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, he said: It was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his return from Hudaybiyyah, and they had been prevented from performing their rituals. He had slaughtered the sacrificial animals at Hudaybiyyah, and his companions were feeling depressed and sad with him. He said, A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the entire world. So he recited, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, * That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come... to His saying, exalted. His companions said, Congratulations, O Messenger of God! God has made clear to us what He will do with you, so what will He do with us? So God revealed this verse after it, That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally... to His saying, And that is, in the sight of God, a great attainment. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Dawud told us: Ibn Hammam told us: Qatada told us on the authority of Anas: This verse was revealed, and he mentioned something similar. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, in a similar manner, except that he said in his hadith: “A man from the people said: ‘Congratulations to you, O Messenger of God.’ He also said: ‘So God explained what He would do to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and what He would do to them.’” Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: "The verse, 'That God may forgive you your sins, past and future,' was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was returning from al-Hudaybiyyah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, 'A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than anything on the earth.' Then he recited it to them, and they said, 'Congratulations and good report, O Prophet of God. God, the Exalted, has explained to you what He did to you, so what will He do with us?' Then the verse, 'That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow' was revealed to him... until His saying, 'a great attainment.'" Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of `Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path, they said, Congratulations and good report for you, O Messenger of God! So what is for us? Then the verse was revealed, That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally, and remove from them their misdeeds. (al-Fath 48:5). Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: I heard Qatada narrating on the authority of Anas regarding this verse: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. He said: Al-Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Aba Awana told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: We did not consider the conquest of Mecca to be anything but the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Abu Kurayb narrated: Ya`la ibn `Ubayd narrated to us, on the authority of `Abd al-`Aziz ibn Siyah, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu Wa`il, who said: “Sahl ibn Hunayf spoke on the day of Siffin and said: ‘O people, accuse yourselves. You saw us on the day of Hudaybiyyah,’ meaning the peace treaty that was between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists. If we had seen fighting, we would have fought. `Umar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, are we not on the right path and they on the wrong path? Aren’t our dead in Paradise and their dead in Hell? ’ He said: ‘Yes. ’ He said: ‘Then why should we give up our religion and go back before God has judged between us and them? ’ He said: ‘O Ibn al-Khattab, I am the Messenger of God, and He will never let me down. ’ He said: ‘So he went back in anger, but he could not be patient until he went to Abu Bakr and said: ‘O Abu Bakr, are we not on the right path and they on the wrong path? Aren’t our dead in Paradise and their dead in Hell? ’ He said: ‘Yes. ’ He said: ‘Then why should we give up our religion and go back before God has judged between us? ’ And among them? He said: O Ibn Al-Khattab, he is the Messenger of God, God will never let him down. He said: So Surat Al-Fath was revealed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to Umar, and he read it to him, and he said: O Messenger of God, was he the conquest? He said: Yes. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: We did not count the conquest except as the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: You consider the conquest to be the conquest of Mecca, but the conquest of Mecca was a conquest. We consider the conquest to be the Pledge of Ridwan on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fifteen hundred. Al-Hudaybiyyah is a well. Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli narrated to me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Isa, who said: Majma' bin Ya'qub al-Ansari narrated to us, who said: I heard my father narrating on the authority of his uncle Abd al-Rahman bin Yazid, on the authority of his uncle Majma' bin Jariyah al-Ansari, who was one of the reciters of the Qur'an. He said: "We were present at al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). When we were turned away from it, the people were urging the camels on. Some of the people said to one another: 'What is wrong with the people?' They said: 'It was revealed to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): 'Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, so that God may forgive you.' A man said: 'Is it a conquest, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'Yes, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, it is a conquest.' Khaybar was divided among the people of al-Hudaybiyyah. No one entered it with them except those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah. The army numbered 1,500, including 300 horsemen. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) divided it into eighteen shares, giving the horsemen two shares and the foot soldiers one share." Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: “The verse, ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest’ was revealed at Al-Hudaybiyyah. In that battle, he achieved what he had not achieved in any other battle. He achieved the Pledge of Ridwan, and he was forgiven for what had happened in the past and in the future. The Romans defeated the Persians, the sacrificial animals reached their destination, and they were fed from the date palms of Khaybar. The believers rejoiced at the confirmation of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and at the Romans’ victory over the Persians.” And the Almighty’s saying: And He completes His favor upon you by making you victorious over your enemy, raising your reputation in this world, and forgiving your sins in the Hereafter. And guides you to a straight path means: He directs you to a path of religion that is free of crookedness, that leads you straight to the pleasure of your Lord. And God will grant you a mighty victory means: He will grant you victory over all your enemies, and over those who oppose you, a victory that no one can overcome and no one can repel, because of the might with which God supports you and the victory with which He provides you.
48:2: God Almighty says: That God may forgive you your sins, past and future, and complete His favor upon you, and guide you to a straight path.
48:3: God Almighty says: And God will grant you a mighty victory.
48:4: God the Most High means by His statement, It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers, that God sent down tranquility and reassurance into the hearts of the believers in God and His Messenger, with faith and the truth with which God sent you, O Muhammad. The difference of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of tranquility has already been mentioned before, and the correct view regarding this is based on evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. So that they may increase in faith along with their faith. He says: So that they may increase in their belief in the new obligations that God has imposed on them, which were not binding on them before. So that they may increase in faith along with their faith. He says: So that they may increase in their belief in the obligations that were binding on them before that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Saleh narrated to us, he said: Muawiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers, he said: Tranquility means mercy, that they might increase in faith along with their [present] faith, he said: Indeed, God, the Most High, sent to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the testimony that there is no god but God. When they believed in it, He increased them in Hajj, then He perfected their religion for them, saying, This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you (5:3). Ibn Abbas said: So the most authentic, true, and perfect faith of the people of the earth and the people of the heavens is the testimony that there is no god but God. And His statement, And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, God Almighty says: And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, supporters by which He takes revenge on whomever He wills of His enemies. And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise, God Almighty says: And God has always had knowledge of what was to come before it came into being, and of what He created, and He is Wise in His management.
48:5: God Almighty says: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, so that you may be grateful to your Lord and praise Him for that, and He will forgive you your past and future sins. And let the believers in God praise their Lord and thank Him for His favor upon them, for the conquest He granted them and decreed between them and their enemies among the polytheists, by making them victorious over them. Thus, He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, and that He will expiate for them their evil deeds with the good deeds they do, as thanks from them to their Lord for what He decreed for them and bestowed upon them. And that is with God a great attainment. God Almighty says: And what God promised them of this promise, that is, their admission to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and His expiation of their evil deeds with the good deeds they do, is with God for them a great attainment. He says: A triumph on their part for what they had hoped for and strove for, and salvation from what they had been fearing of a great punishment from God. It was previously mentioned that this verse was revealed when the believers said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or he recited to them the words of God Almighty: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow. This is for you, O Messenger of God, so what is for us? It is a clarification from God to them of what He will do with them. Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow...to His statement, and remove from them their misdeeds. So God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. His saying, That the believing men and women may enter is based on the lam of his saying, That God may forgive you what came before of your sin, with the interpretation of repeating the statement, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest * That God may forgive you, Indeed, We have granted you that the believing men and women may enter gardens beneath which rivers flow. For this reason, the waw that is entered into the statement for the purpose of conjunction was not used, so He did not say, And that the believing men and women may enter.
48:6: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you and admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and that He may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, by God’s granting to you, O Muhammad, what He has granted you of victory over the polytheists of Quraysh.” So they will be saddened by that and their hopes will be disappointed, which they had hoped to see in the people of faith in you of weakness and various forms of turning away from you in this worldly life, and burning in the Fire and remaining in it forever in the Hereafter. And the polytheistic men and polytheistic women, He says: And He will likewise punish the polytheistic men and polytheistic women who think of God that He will not grant you victory and the people of faith in you over your enemies, and that He will not make His word prevail and make it supreme over the word of the disbelievers in Him. This was the evil of their suspicions that God mentioned in this place. God Almighty says: Upon the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists who suspected the circle of evil, meaning the circle of torment would revolve around them. The reciters differed in their recitation of this word. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Da’irat al-Su’ with a fat-ha on the seen. Some of the reciters of Basra read it as Da’irat al-Su’ with a damma on the seen. Al-Farra’ used to say: The fat-ha is more widespread in the seen. He said: The Arabs rarely say Da’irat al-Su’ with a damma on the seen. The fat-ha on the seen is more pleasing to me than the damma, because the Arabs say: He is a bad man with a fat-ha on the seen, but they do not say: He is a bad man. And His statement, And God’s wrath was upon them, means that God became angry with them and cursed them, meaning that He distanced them and removed them from His mercy. And prepared Hell for them, means that He prepared Hell for them, which they will burn in on the Day of Resurrection. And evil is the destination, means that Hell is evil as a home to which these hypocrites, men and women, and polytheists, men and women, will end up.
48:7: And His statement, And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, God Almighty says: And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth as helpers against His enemies. If He commands them to destroy them, they destroy them, and they hasten to do so out of obedience to Him. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, God Almighty says: And God has always been Exalted in Might, and no one can overcome Him, and no one can prevent Him from doing what He wants, due to the greatness of His authority and power. He is Wise in His management of His creation.
48:8: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Indeed, We have sent you, O Muhammad, as a witness over your nation regarding what they responded to in what you called them to, in what I sent you to them of the message, and as a bearer of good tidings” to them of Paradise if they responded to what you called them to of the upright religion, and as a warner to them of the punishment of God if they turn away from what you brought them from your Lord.
48:9: Then the reading differed in his statement, That you may believe in God and His Messenger and honor him and respect him and glorify Him. The majority of the readers of the regions, except for Abu Ja`far al-Madani and Abu `Amr ibn al-`Ala’, read all of it with a ta’, li-ya-yi... The correct thing to say about this is: They are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner, meaning: a witness to his nation that he has conveyed the message to them and a bringer of good tidings of Paradise for those who obey God, and a warner of the Fire. And his saying, And you honor him and respect him, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: You honor him and respect him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they honor him means: reverence and they respect him means: glorify. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid informed us. He said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And they honor him and respect him, all of this is glorification and reverence. Others said: The meaning of his saying and they honor him is and they support him, and the meaning is and they respect him and they magnify him. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qada: And they support him means they support him and respect him. God commanded that he be made black and glorified. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, and they support him, he said: They support him and honor him, meaning they glorify him. Abu Hurairah Al-Dab’i told me: Harami told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr Ja’far bin Abi Wahshiyyah, on the authority of Ikrimah, and they punish him. He said: They fight with him with the sword. Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told me on the authority of Abu Bishr on the authority of Ikrimah, similarly. Ahmad bin Al-Walid told me: Uthman bin Omar told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ikrimah, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya and Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ikrimah, similarly. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd told us regarding His statement, And they honor him and respect him, he said: Obedience is to God. These sayings are similar in meaning, although their wording differs. The meaning of ta'zir in this context is strengthening through support and assistance, and this can only be achieved through obedience, reverence, and veneration. We have explained the meaning of this with evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. As for reverence: it is glorification, veneration and magnification. His statement, And glorify Him in the morning and the evening, means: And pray to Him, meaning to God in the mornings and evenings. The ha in His statement, And glorify Him, refers to the mention of God alone, not the Messenger. It has been mentioned that this is in some readings: And glorify God in the morning and the evening. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, And they glorify Him in the morning and the evening, in some of the recitations, And they glorify God in the morning and the evening. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding some of the letters: And they glorify God morning and evening. I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And they glorify Him morning and evening, meaning: They glorify God. He returned to himself.
48:10: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Those of your companions who pledge allegiance to you at Al-Hudaibiyah, on the condition that they will not flee when meeting the enemy, nor turn their backs to them, are only pledging allegiance to God. He says: They are only pledging their allegiance to you to God, because God has guaranteed them Paradise through their companionship with Him in that regard. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Those who pledge allegiance to you, he said: On the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to God. The hand of God is over their hands. So whoever breaks his pledge only breaks it to the detriment of his own soul.” They are those who pledged allegiance on the day of Hudaybiyyah. And in His saying, The hand of God is above their hands, there are two aspects of interpretation: One of them: The hand of God is above their hands at the time of the pledge of allegiance, because they were pledging allegiance to God by their pledge of allegiance to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the other: The power of God is above their power in supporting His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they only pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to support him against the enemy. And His statement, But whoever breaks his pledge, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself, God Almighty says: So whoever breaks his pledge to you, O Muhammad, and breaks it and does not support you against your enemies, and goes against what his Lord promised, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself, meaning: He only breaks his pledge because by doing that he is excluded from those to whom God promised Paradise for fulfilling the pledge. So his breaking of the pledge did not harm anyone but himself, and he only broke it to himself. As for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God Almighty supported him against his enemies, whether the one who broke the pledge among them broke it or fulfilled his pledge. And His statement, And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God, the verse, the Almighty says: And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God of patience when meeting the enemy in the way of God, supporting His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against his enemies, then He will give him a great reward, meaning: God will give him a great reward, and that is that He will admit him into Paradise as a reward for his fulfillment of what he pledged to God, and his trust in His Messenger to be patient with him during times of hardship, with the confirmation of faith. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who told you: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Then He will give him a great reward, meaning Paradise.
48:11: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “O Muhammad, those whom God has left behind with their families, who did not accompany you and did not go out with you on your journey that you took, and the journey that you took to Mecca to perform Umrah, visiting the Sacred House of God, will say to you, if you return to them and rebuke them for staying behind you: We were distracted from going out with you by dealing with our money, and improving our livelihoods and our families, so ask forgiveness for us, our Lord, for staying behind you.” God Almighty says, refuting their statement: These Bedouins who stayed behind say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, and that is their asking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask forgiveness for them. He says: They ask Him without repentance from them or regret for what they have done in their past of disobeying God in staying behind from the company of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the journey from him. “Say: Then who can control for you anything from God?” God Almighty says to His Prophet: Say to these Bedouins who ask you to ask forgiveness for them for staying behind you: If I… I seek forgiveness for you, O people. Then God willed your destruction or the destruction of your wealth and your families, or He willed to benefit you by making your wealth flourish and your families better. So who is able to repel what God willed for you of good or evil? No one can defeat God, and no one can overcome Him. And His statement, Rather, God is All-Aware of what you do, means, the Most High says: “What is the matter with you, as these hypocrites among the Bedouins think, that God does not know what they are doing in terms of hypocrisy? Rather, God has always been All-Aware of what they do, good and evil. Nothing of the deeds of His creation, whether secret or public, is hidden from Him. He is recording them until He rewards them for them.” And it was reported that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) wanted to go to Mecca in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah to perform Umrah, he mobilized the Arabs and the Bedouins around his city to go out with him, for fear that his people, the Quraysh, would expose him to war or prevent him from entering the House. He (blessings and peace of God be upon him) entered ihram for Umrah and brought sacrificial animals with him to show the people that he did not want to wage war. However, many of the Bedouins were reluctant to go with him and stayed behind. They are the ones whom God, the Most High, meant when He said, Those of the Bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, ‘Our wealth and our families have occupied us…’… And what we said about this was said by the people of knowledge of the biography of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his campaigns, including Ibn Ishaq. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the same authority. Muhammad ibn Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Those of the bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, ‘Our wealth and our families have preoccupied us.’ He said: The bedouins of Medina: Juhayna and Muzayna. He followed them to go out to Mecca. They said: We will go with him to a people who came to him and killed his companions, so we can fight them. They made excuses for being preoccupied. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase if He intended to harm you. The reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, read it as dharana with a fatha on the letter dhad, meaning harm that is the opposite of benefit. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as dharana with a damma on the letter dhad, meaning misery and illness. The most amazing of the two readings is the opening of the letter Ḍād in this place, in his saying, Or He intended to benefit you. It is known that the opposite of benefit and harm is true, even if the other has a correct meaning.
48:12: God Almighty says to these Bedouins who apologized to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he returned from his journey to them, saying, Our wealth and our families distracted us. You did not stay behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he departed from you, and you did not accompany him because you were busy with your wealth and your families. Rather, you stayed behind in your homes after him, thinking that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those of his companions who were with him would perish and never return to you again because the enemy had exterminated them. This was made attractive to you, and Satan made it seem good to you, and he made it sound right to you until staying behind him seemed attractive to you, so you stayed away from his company. And you thought an evil thought, meaning: You thought that God would not grant victory to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his believing companions over their enemies, and that the enemy would subjugate them and overcome them and kill them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, The bedouins who stayed behind will say to you… until his statement, And you were a people who were ruined. He said: They thought about the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions that they would not return from that destination, and that they would perish, so that is what kept them from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And his saying, And you were a people who were ruined, means: And you were a people who were doomed and not fit for any good. It was said that bur in the language of Adhra’at means corrupt, but among the Arabs it means nothing. And from this is the saying of Abu Darda’: So what they had gathered became bur meaning gone and became worthless and nothing of it. And from this is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit: Length is of no use to those who have broken hearts. God may guide the path of the barren group. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And you were a people who were corrupt, he said: corrupt. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And you were a barren people, he said: Barrenness is that in which there is no goodness. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you were a people of desolation, he said: Desolation is that in which there is no goodness. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you were a people who were lost, he said: perished.
48:13: God the Most High says to these hypocrites from among the Bedouins: And whoever does not believe, O bedouins, in God and His Messenger, from among you and from others, and does not believe in what he has been told, and acknowledges what he brought of the truth from his Lord, then We have prepared for them all a Blaze of Fire that will blaze against them in Hell when they enter it on the Day of Resurrection. It is said of this: I kindled the fire, if you lit it, so I kindle it with a blaze. It is also said: I stirred it, if you moved it. The one who kindles the fire is called a kindler because he stirs the fire with it. From this is their saying: He kindles war, meaning he who kindles it and incites it.
48:14: And His statement, And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, God Almighty says: And to God belongs the authority of the heavens and the earth, so no one, O hypocrites, will be able to prevent Him from what He intended to punish you for your hypocrisy if you persist in it, or to prevent Him from pardoning you if He pardons you, if you repent from your hypocrisy and disbelief. This is from God, the Most High, urging these Bedouins who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to repent and return to God’s command in obeying His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says to them: Hasten to repent for staying behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for God forgives those who repent. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, He says: And God has always been forgiving of the punishment of those of His servants who repent to Him for their sins and transgressions, and He is merciful to them by punishing them for their sins after they repent from them.
48:15: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: “O Muhammad, those who stayed behind with their families and did not accompany you when you set out on your pilgrimage, intending to visit the Sacred House of God, will say: When you and your companions set out on your journey to what God has bestowed upon you and them of spoils, “to take them,” and that is what God had promised the people of Hudaybiyyah from the spoils of Khaybar, Leave us to follow you to Khaybar, so that we may witness with you the fighting of its people. They want to change the word of God. He says: They want to change the promise of God that He promised the people of Hudaybiyyah, and that is because God had given them the spoils of Khaybar, and He promised them that in exchange for the spoils of the people of Mecca if you left them in a peace treaty, and they did not take anything from them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Mecca, and God promised him many spoils, so Khaybar was made his. Then those who stayed behind said, Leave us to follow you, wanting to change the word of God. They were the spoils to take, about which God, the Most High, said: When you set out to take spoils, and they were offered to fight a people of great strength. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of a man from his companions, on the authority of Muqsim, who said: When God promised them that He would conquer Khaybar for them, and God had promised it to those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah, He did not give anything of it to anyone other than them. When the hypocrites knew that it was the spoils, they said, Leave us to follow you, wanting to change the words of God. He said, What He had promised them. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Those who stayed behind will say when you set out... The verse refers to those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Hudaybiyyah. It was mentioned to us that when the polytheists prevented the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Hudaybiyyah, from the Sacred Mosque and the sacrificial animals, Al-Miqdad said: “O Prophet of God, by God, we do not say like the leaders of the Children of Israel when they said to their Prophet: ‘Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.’ Rather, we say: ‘Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are fighting with you.’ When the companions of the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard that, they pledged allegiance to what he had said. When the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw that, he made peace with the Quraysh, and most of them returned.” Others said: Rather, what he meant by his saying, They want to change the words of God, is their desire to go out with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his conquest. God Almighty said, Then say, ‘You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy.’ (al-Tawbah 9:83). Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God, Those who stayed behind will say, ‘When you set out to take the spoils, “Leave us, we will follow you… the verse, God, the Almighty, said to him when he returned from a raid, “And they asked your permission to go out. Say, ‘You will never go out.’ Say, ‘You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me against an enemy.’” the verse. They wanted to change the words of God: they wanted to change the words of God that He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to go out with him, but God, may He be exalted, refused that to them and to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what Ibn Zayd said, a statement that has no basis, because the words of God Almighty And they asked your permission to go out, so say, You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy were revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon his return from Tabuk, and He meant by it those who stayed behind when he headed to Tabuk to fight the Romans. There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge about the campaigns of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Tabuk was after the conquest of Khaybar and was also considered the conquest of Mecca. So how can the matter be as we have described, meant by the words of God, They want to change the word of God? This is report about those who stayed behind from traveling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he set out on a pilgrimage, intending to perform the minor pilgrimage, and the polytheists who stayed behind from him in the Battle of Tabuk prevented him from going to the House. The Battle of Tabuk did not take place on the day this verse was revealed, nor was the words And they asked your permission to go out, so say, You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If that is the case, then the correct thing to say about it is what Mujahid and Qatada said, as we have explained. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, They want to change the Word of God. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, read it as the Word of God as a verbal noun, with the alif added. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as the Word of God without an alif, meaning the plural of a word. We believe that these are two widely used readings in the regions, and they are close in meaning. Whichever one the reciter reads, he is correct, although I am more inclined to read it with the alif. And His statement, “Say, ‘You will not follow us. Thus did God say before.’” God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say to those who stayed behind from the journey with you, O Muhammad: You will not follow us to Khaybar if we want to go to them to fight them. Thus did God say before. He says: Thus did God say to us before our return to you, that the spoils of Khaybar are for those who witnessed Hudaybiyyah with us, and you are not among those who witnessed it, so it is not for you to follow us to Khaybar, because its spoils are for someone other than you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Thus said God before, meaning that the spoils of war were only made for the people of jihad, and the spoils of war of Khaybar were only for those who witnessed Hudaybiyyah, and no one else had a share in them. And His saying, Then they will say, ‘Rather, you envy us,’ that we would gain a share of booty with you if we testified with you, and that is why they prevent us from going out with you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this. Those who said this mentioned: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Then they will say, ‘Rather, you envy us,’ that we share spoils with you. And His statement, Rather, they did not understand except a little, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions: The matter is not as these hypocrites among the Bedouins say, that you only prevent them from following you out of envy of them so that they may obtain booty with you from the enemy. Rather, they did not understand from God what they had to do with and against them in the matter of religion except a little. If they had understood that, they would not have said to the Messenger of God and the believers in him, even though they had informed them from God Almighty that He had forbidden them the spoils of Khaybar. You only prevent us from accompanying you to it because you envy us.
48:16: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the Bedouins who stayed behind from the journey with you, ‘You will be called to fight a people of great strength in fighting.’ The commentators differed regarding those about whom God Almighty said that these Bedouins who stayed behind were called to fight. Some of them said: They are the people of Persia. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Of great strength means the people of Persia. Ismail bin Musa Al-Fazari told us: Dawud bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Banani, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, regarding his statement, You will be called to a people of great strength, he said: The Persians and the Romans. He said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada who said: Al-Hasan, in his statement, You will be called to a people of great strength, said: They are the Persians of Rome. Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Of great strength, he said: They are the Persians. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: You will be called to a people of great strength. He said: Al-Hasan said: They will be called to the Persians and the Romans. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, You will be called to a people of great strength, he said: Persia and Rome. Others said: They are Hawazin of Hunayn. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Abu Bishr told us on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah regarding his statement, You will be called to a people of great strength, he said: Hawazin and Thaqif. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: Of great strength, you fight them or they surrender. He said: They are Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: “Say to those of the Bedouins who stayed behind: You will be called to fight a people of great strength.” So they were called on the day of Hunayn to fight Hawazin and Thaqif, and some of them responded well and were eager to fight. Others said: Rather, they are Banu Hanifa. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri: Those of great strength. He said: The Banu Hanifa with Musaylimah the Liar. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah, that they used to add to it Hawazin and Banu Hanifa. Others said: This verse has not come yet. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: You will be called to fight against a people of great strength. This verse did not come. Others said: They are the Romans. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Awf told me: Abu al-Mughira told us: Sufyan ibn Amr told us: Al-Faraj ibn Muhammad al-Kila’i told us on the authority of Ka’b, who said: Those of great strength means the Romans. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty informed us about those Arabs who stayed behind that they would be called to fight a people who were brave in fighting and courageous in wars, and he did not make clear to us the evidence from the report or reason that what was meant by that was Hawazin, nor Banu Hanifa, nor Persia, nor the Romans, nor any notables in particular. It is possible that what was meant by that was some of these races, and it is possible that what was meant by them was someone other than them, and there is no saying about it that is more correct than to say as God Almighty said: They will be called to fight a people who were very brave. And His statement, You fight them or they submit, God Almighty says to the sworn Arabs: You fight these whom you call to fight, or they submit without war or fighting. It has been mentioned that in some readings it is: You fight them until they surrender. According to this reading - even though it is contrary to the copies of the Qur’an of the people of the regions, and contrary to what the proof of the reciters is upon, and it is not permissible for me to recite it accordingly - the interpretation of that is: You fight them forever until they surrender, or until they surrender. And His statement, If you obey, God will give you a good reward, means that if you obey God in responding to Him when He calls you to fight these people of great strength, and you respond to fighting them and jihad alongside the believers, God will give you a good reward, meaning that God will give you Paradise for responding to your response to fighting them, which is the good reward. But if you turn away as you turned away before, meaning, if you disobey your Lord and turn away from obeying Him and disobeying His command and abandoning fighting those of great strength when you are called to fight them, He will punish you with a painful punishment, meaning painfully, and that is the punishment of the Fire for your disobedience to Him and your abandoning jihad and fighting them alongside the believers.
48:17: God Almighty says: There is no hardship upon the blind among you, O people, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, that they should stay behind from jihad with the believers, and witness war with them when they meet their enemy, due to the ailments that they have, and the reasons that prevent them from witnessing it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick. He said: All of this is in jihad. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, who said: Then God excused those who have an excuse among the people, and said: There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the ill. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the ill, he said: In jihad in the way of God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: There is no blame upon the blind… the verse, meaning in fighting. And His statement, And whoever obeys God and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. God Almighty says: And whoever obeys God and His Messenger and responds to the war against the enemies of God from among the polytheists, and to fight with the believers, seeking the countenance of God when called to that, God will admit him on the Day of Resurrection to gardens beneath which rivers flow. And whoever turns away. He says: And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger, and refrains from fighting the polytheists with God when called to that, and does not respond to the call of God and His Messenger - He will punish him with a painful punishment, and that is the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection.
48:18: God Almighty says: God was pleased, O Muhammad, with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. Meaning the pledge of allegiance of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Messenger of God at Al-Hudaybiyah when they pledged allegiance to him to fight the Quraysh in the war, and not to flee or turn their backs to them under the tree. Their pledge of allegiance to him there, as mentioned, was under a tree. The reason for this pledge of allegiance is what was said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, with his message to the leaders of Quraysh, and Uthman was somewhat slow in responding to him, so he thought that he had been killed. So he called his companions to renew the pledge of allegiance to their war as I have described, so they pledged allegiance to him on that. This pledge is called the Pledge of Ridwan, and those who pledged allegiance to him in this pledge were, according to what was mentioned by some of them: one thousand four hundred, and according to some of them: one thousand five hundred, and according to some of them: one thousand three hundred. Mentioning the narration of what we described as the reason for this pledge: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: “Some of the people of knowledge told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Khurash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza’i and sent him to the Quraysh in Mecca, and carried him on his camel called al-Thalab, to convey to their leaders what he had come to him for. That was when he had arrived at al-Hudaybiyyah, and they hamstrung the Messenger of God’s camel, may God bless him and grant him peace, and wanted to kill him, but the Abyssinians prevented them and let him go until he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” He said: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not accuse told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Mecca to inform the nobles of what he had come for. He said: O Messenger of God, I fear for myself from the Quraysh, and there is no one in Mecca from the Banu Adi ibn Ka’b to protect me. The Quraysh know my hostility towards them and my harshness towards them, but I will direct you to a man who is more honored there than I am: Uthman ibn Affan. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of the Quraysh to inform them that he had not come to fight, but had come to visit this House, respecting its sanctity. Uthman went out to Mecca, and Aban ibn Sa’id ibn al-As met him when he entered Mecca or before he entered it. He got down from his mount and carried him in front of him, then rode behind him and protected him until he delivered the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Uthman set out until he reached Abu Sufyan and the nobles of the Quraysh, and informed them of what he had come to say.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not send him with it. They said to Uthman when he had finished sending the message to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it. He said: I would not do that until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulates it. So the Quraysh considered it a reward for them, and the report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims reached him that Uthman had been killed. He said: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Abdullah ibn Bakr narrated to me that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard that Uthman had been killed, he said: We will not leave until we fight the people. He called the people to the pledge of allegiance, so the Pledge of Ridwan took place under the tree. The people were saying: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave them a pledge of allegiance to death. Jabir ibn Abdullah used to say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not give us a pledge of allegiance to death, but he gave us a pledge that we would not flee. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave the people a pledge of allegiance, and none of the Muslims who were present stayed behind except Al-Jadd ibn Qays, the brother of Ibn Salamah. Jabir ibn Abdullah used to say: It is as if I can see him clinging to the armpit of his camel, hiding behind it from the people. Then he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said that what was mentioned about Uthman was false. Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi narrated: Ubaidullah bin Musa narrated: Musa bin Ubaidah narrated on the authority of Iyas bin Salamah, who said: Salamah said: “While we were saying the Pledge of Allegiance at the time of Al-Hudaybiyyah, the herald of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out: ‘O people, pledge allegiance! The Holy Spirit, may God’s prayers be upon him, has descended.’ He said: So we went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was under a samura tree. He said: So we pledged allegiance to him, and that is the statement of God: ‘God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree.’” Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Yashkari told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Amer, who said: The first person to pledge allegiance to Ridwan was a man from Banu Asad called Abu Sinan bin Wahb. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: My grandfather was called Hazn, and he was among those who pledged allegiance under the tree. We came to it the following year, but it was hidden from us. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr bin Al-Harith told me on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Ashja: “It reached him that the people had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to die, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘For as much as you are able.’ The tree under which the pledge of allegiance was pledged was in a valley towards Mecca. They claimed that Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him passed by that place after the tree had disappeared, and he said: ‘Where was it?’ Some of them said: ‘Here,’ and some of them said: ‘Here.’ When their disagreement increased, he said: ‘Go on, this is how we are doing.’ So the tree disappeared, and it had been a tamarisk tree, either a flood had taken it away or something else.” Mention the number of those who pledged allegiance to this pledge. We have mentioned the differences among those who differed regarding their number, and we will mention the narrations of those who said the articles that we mentioned, God willing. It was mentioned that their number was one thousand four hundred. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “On the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, we were one thousand and four hundred. We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that we would not flee, but we did not pledge allegiance to him to die. He said: So we all pledged allegiance to him except Al-Jadd bin Qais, who hid under the armpit of his camel.” Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd told me: Al-Qasim ibn Abdullah ibn Amr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah: “On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, they were fourteen hundred. We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) while Umar was holding him by the hand under a samura tree. No one pledged allegiance to us except al-Jadd ibn Qays al-Ansari, who hid under the armpit of his camel. Jabir said: We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) that we would not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him to die.” Yusuf bin Musa al-Qattan told us: Hisham bin Abdul Malik and Saeed bin Shurahbil al-Masry told us: Layth bin Saad al-Masry told us: Abu al-Zubayr told us on the authority of Jabir, who said: “On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, we were one thousand and four hundred, so we pledged allegiance to him and Umar was holding his hand under the tamarisk tree, so we pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee, and that we would not pledge allegiance to him to die, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that it was said to him: Jaber bin Abdullah says: The people of the tree were one thousand five hundred. Saeed said: Jaber forgot. He told me that they were one thousand four hundred. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: We were fourteen hundred people at Al-Hudaybiyyah. It was mentioned that they were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five. Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He said: The people who pledged allegiance under the tree were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree, and the spoils of Khaybar were given to them, were fifteen hundred on that day, and they pledged allegiance that they would not flee from him. It was mentioned that they were one thousand and three hundred. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Amr bin Murrah: He heard Abdullah bin Abi Awfa say: On the Day of the Tree they were one thousand and three hundred, and Aslam was among the emigrants on that day. And His statement, He knew what was in their hearts, means that God Almighty says: So your Lord knew, O Muhammad, what was in the hearts of the believers among your companions when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, of sincerity of intention, fulfillment of what they pledged to you, and patience with you. So He sent down tranquility upon them, meaning: So He sent down reassurance, steadfastness in their religion, and good insight into the truth to which God guided them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Then He knew what was in their hearts and sent down tranquility upon them: meaning patience and dignity. His statement, And He rewarded them with an imminent conquest, means: He compensated them in the immediate future for what they had hoped to obtain from the spoils of the people of Mecca by fighting its people with an imminent conquest. And that, as it was said, was the conquest of Khaybar. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla: And He rewarded them with an imminent conquest. He said: Khaybar. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And He rewarded them with an imminent conquest, which is Khaybar. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And He rewarded them with an imminent conquest. He said: I was informed that it was Khaybar. And His statement, And they will take many spoils, means that God Almighty says: And God rewarded those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree, along with what He honored them with in His pleasure with them, and His sending down tranquility upon them, and His establishing for them an imminent conquest, with many spoils that they will take from the wealth of the Jews of Khaybar, for God made that specific to the people of the Pledge of Ridwan and not to others. And His saying, And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, means: And God is Exalted in Might in taking revenge on those who took revenge on His enemies, and Wise in His management of His creation and disposing of them as He wills of His judgment.
48:19: God Almighty says: “And they will take many spoils. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.”
48:20: God Almighty says to the people of the Pledge of Ridwan: God has promised you, O people, many spoils that you will take. The people of interpretation differed regarding these spoils that God mentioned that He promised to these people, which spoils they are. Some of them said: They are all the spoils that God gave to the believers in Him from the wealth of the polytheists since He revealed this verse through the tongue of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, God has promised you abundant spoils that you will take. He said: The abundant spoils that they were promised: they have not taken them to this day. According to this interpretation, the statement may mean that what is meant by the second spoils is the first spoils, and its meaning then would be: So He rewarded them with an imminent victory, and abundant spoils that they would take. God has promised you, O people, these spoils that you will take, and you are continuing to them, so He made for you the imminent victory from the conquest of Khaybar. It may also be that the second is not the first, and the first is from the spoils of Khaybar and the second spoils that He promised them were from the spoils of all the polytheists other than them. Others said: These spoils that God promised these people are the spoils of Khaybar. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, God has promised you many spoils that you will take, he said: On the day of Khaybar. He said: My father used to say that. And his saying, So He hastened this for you. The people of interpretation differed as to what was hastened for them. A group said: The spoils of Khaybar, and the remainder are all the conquests of the Muslims after that time until the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So He hastened this for you. He said: He hastened this for you, an expert. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So he hastened this for you, which refers to Khaybar. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was the peace treaty that took place between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Quraysh. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So he hastened this for you, he said: The peace. The first of the correct interpretations of this is what Mujahid said, which is that what God rewarded them for their march along with the recent conquest was the many spoils of Khaybar. This is because the Muslims did not seize any spoils after Hudaybiyyah, and they did not achieve a conquest closer to it than their pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Hudaybiyyah, which was closer to the conquest of Khaybar and its spoils. As for his saying, God has promised you many spoils, they are all the spoils that God granted them after Khaybar, such as the spoils of Hawazin, Ghatafan, Persia, and Rome. We said this in this way, without the spoils of Khaybar, because God informed us that He hastened for them this reward for their journey that they took with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Mecca, and because He knew of the sincerity of their intention to fight its people, as they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they would not flee from him. There is no doubt that what was hastened for them was not what was not hastened for them. And His saying, And He restrained the hands of the people from you, means that God Almighty says to the people of the Pledge of Ridwan: And God restrained the hands of the polytheists from you. Then the people of interpretation differed about who were those whose hands were restrained from them? Some of them said: They are the Jews whose hands were restrained from the families of those who traveled from Medina with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Mecca. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And restrain the hands of people from you: from their homes and from their families in Medina when they marched to Al-Hudaybiyyah and to Khaybar, and Khaybar was in that direction. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And restrain the hands of people from you, he said: Restrain the hands of people from their families in Medina. Others said: Rather, he meant the hands of the Quraysh, as God kept them away from him, so they were unable to harm him. What Qatada said about this, in my opinion, is more similar to the interpretation of the verse, and that is that God’s restraining of the hands of the polytheists of the people of Mecca from the people of Al-Hudaybiyyah was mentioned by God after this verse in His statement, And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca. So it is known from this that the restraining that God Almighty mentioned in His statement, And restrained the hands of the people from you, is different from the restraining that God mentioned after this verse in His statement, And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca. And His statement, And that it may be a sign for the believers, means: And that His, the Most High, restraining their hands from their families may be a sign and a lesson for those who believe in Him, so that they may know that God is the One who protects and cares for them, when they are present and when they are absent, and they may fear God in themselves, their wealth, and their families by preserving and maintaining good guardianship as long as they are steadfast in His obedience, abiding by His commands and prohibitions. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And that it may be a sign to the believers, meaning that people will keep their hands off their families. And guide you to a straight path, meaning that He will direct you, O believers, to a clear path with no crookedness in it, and He will make it clear to you, which is that you should trust in your Lord in all your affairs, and rely on Him in all of them, so that He may protect you as He protected you on your journey to Mecca with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in yourselves, your families, and your wealth. You have seen the effect of God’s action with you, since you trusted in this journey of yours.
48:21: And His statement, And another which you were not able to conquer, God has encompassed it. God Almighty says, And your Lord has promised you, O people, that He will open another city which you were not able to conquer, and God has encompassed it for you until He opens it for you. The people of interpretation differed regarding this other town and the village that he promised them to conquer, which he told them he would surround. Some of them said: It is the land of Persia and Rome, and whatever lands the Muslims conquer until the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Samak Al-Hanafi: I heard Ibn Abbas say: And another that you were not able to control means Persia and Rome. He said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla, that he said regarding this verse: And another which you have no power over, he said: Persia and Rome. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Zaid bin Habbab told us: Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Ibn Abi Laila, the same. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And another which you have no power over, God has encompassed it. He said: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It is Persia and Rome. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And another that you have not been able to conquer, they have not conquered until today. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, regarding his statement, And another that you have no power over, he said: Persia and Rome. Others said: Rather, it is Khaybar. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And another which you have not been able to attain...the verse. He said: It is Khaybar. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: “I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, ‘And another which you have no power over, God has encompassed it,’ meaning Khaybar. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them on that day and said: Do not mutilate, do not steal, and do not kill a child.” Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And another which you have no power over, God has encompassed it, he said: Khaybar. He said: They did not mention it nor did they hope for it until God informed them of it. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And another that you were not able to reach, meaning the people of Khaybar. Others said: Rather, it is Mecca. Who said that?
