Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And another which you have not been able to attain, but God has encompassed it. We were told that it was Mecca. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And another which you were not able to reach. He said: We were informed that it was Mecca. This statement made by Qatada is more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, and that is that God informed those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree, that it surrounded a city that they were unable to conquer. It is reasonable that it cannot be said of a people that they were unable to conquer this city, unless they had aimed at it but it was impossible for them. As for them not aiming at it and it was impossible for them, then it cannot be said that they were unable to conquer it. If this is the case, and it is known that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not intend Khaybar for war before this verse was revealed to him, nor did he head there to fight its people with an army or a raiding party, then it is known that what is meant by his saying, And another which you were not able to defeat, is something else, and that it is the one he had tried and sought but was unable to do so, so Mecca and its people were like that, and God, may He be exalted, informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers that He had encompassed it and its people, and that He had conquered it for them, and God has power over all things that He wills, and nothing that He wills is impossible for Him.
48:22: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the people of the Pledge of Ridwan: And if those who disbelieve fight you O believers in Mecca, they will turn their backs meaning: they will flee from you, so they will turn their backs on you, and this is what happens when a person flees from his side in war. Then they will find neither protector nor helper meaning: Then these disbelievers who fled from you, who turned their backs to you, will find neither a protector to befriend them in your war, nor a helper to aid them against you, because God Almighty is with you, and God’s party will not defeat its helper. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And if those who disbelieve should fight you, they would turn their backs, meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh. God said, Then they will find neither protector nor helper, to support them from God.
48:23: And His statement, The way of God which has already been in effect means that God, the Exalted, says: If these infidels from Quraysh had fought you, God would have abandoned them until He defeated them from you as He abandoned their likes from among the people of disbelief in Him, who fought His allies from among the nations who passed before them. And He brought out His statement, The way of God in the accusative case from a different wording, because in His statement, They will turn their backs and then find neither protector nor helper there is a meaning that defeat and abandonment were established for them. Therefore it was said, The way of God is a verbal noun from the meaning of the statement, not from its wording. And it may be permissible for it to be an explanation of what preceded it from the statement. And His saying, And you will not find any change in the way of God, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And you will not find, O Muhammad, any change in the way of God that He established for His creation. Rather, it is permanent. For goodness is rewarded with goodness, and for evil and disbelief is punishment and humiliation.
48:24: God the Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those who pledged the Pledge of Ridwan: And it is He who restrained their hands from you. Meaning that God restrained the hands of the polytheists who had rebelled against the army of God’s Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Hudaybiyyah, seeking to catch them by surprise and kill them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent and brought them as prisoners. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, released them, and was merciful to them and did not kill them. So God said to the believers: And it is He who restrained the hands of these polytheists from you, and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca, after He had given you victory over them. The traces came in a similar manner to what we said. The narration mentioned that: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated: I heard my father say: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated: Thabit al-Banani narrated to me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting at the base of a tree in al-Hudaibiyah, and on his back was a branch of the tree, so I removed it from his back, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, was in front of him and Suhayl ibn Amr, the companion of the polytheists. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: Write, ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.’ Suhayl held his hand and said: ‘We do not know the Most Gracious. Write in our case what we know.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Write, in Your name, O God.’ So he wrote and said: ‘This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, made peace with the people of Mecca.’ Suhayl held his hand and said: ‘We have wronged you, if you are a messenger. Write in our case what we know.’ He said: ‘Write, ‘This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib made peace with, and I am the Messenger of God.’ Then thirty young men wearing weapons came out against us and attacked us. The Messenger of God, may God bless them and grant them peace, invoked curses upon them, and God took away their sight. So we went to them and captured them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you go out under the protection of anyone? He said: So he let them go. He said: Then God revealed: “And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them.” Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya ibn Wadh told us: Al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: “We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Hudaibiyah at the base of the tree of which God mentioned in the Qur’an. There was a branch of that tree on the back of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I lifted it off his back.” Then he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not accuse narrated to me on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, that the Quraysh had sent forty or fifty men from among them and ordered them to go around the camp of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to capture one of his companions. They seized them and brought them to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who pardoned them and let them go. They had thrown stones and arrows at the camp of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Humayd said: Salamah said: Ibn Ishaq said: Concerning this, God said: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them… the verse. Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Husayn told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to perform Umrah, and his companions seized some people from the people of the Sacred Sanctuary, who were unaware. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, let them go, and that was the capture of the valley of Mecca. Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: Ubayd God ibn Aisha told us: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from Mount al-Tan’im, after the dawn prayer, to kill them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took them and set them free, and then God revealed, And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them… the verse. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr narrated to us: Yazid Saeed narrated to us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them… the verse. He said: “The valley of Hudaybiyyah in Mecca is called Ruhm. It went up the pass of Hudaybiyyah, and the polytheists shot him with an arrow and killed him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent cavalry, and they brought him twelve horsemen from the infidels. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Do you have a covenant with me? Do you have a protection with me? They said: No. So he sent them, and God revealed about that the Qur’an: “And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them”… the verse until His saying: He is Seeing of what you do. Others said about this: Ibn Hamid narrated to us: Ya`qub al-Qummi narrated to us on the authority of Ja`far on the authority of Ibn Abza who said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with the sacrificial offerings and reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, `Umar said to him: ‘O Prophet of God, are you entering upon a people with whom you are at war without a weapon or a mount? ’ So he sent to Medina, and he did not leave a mount or a weapon without carrying it. When he approached Mecca, they prevented him from entering, so he marched until he came to Mina. He stopped at Mina, and a vision reached him that `Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl had come out against us with five hundred men. So he said to Khalid, ‘This is your cousin who has come to you with the cavalry. ’ Khalid said, ‘I am the sword of God and the sword of His Messenger - and at that time he was called the sword of God - O Messenger of God, shoot me wherever you wish. ’ So he sent him on cavalry, and he met `Ikrimah in the valley and defeated him until he brought him into the walls of Mecca. Then he returned a second time and defeated him until he brought him into the walls of Mecca. Then he returned a third time and defeated him until he brought him into the walls of Mecca. Then God revealed, ‘And it is He who has restrained their hands from you. ’” And your hands from them...” until His saying, a painful punishment. He said: So God restrained the Prophet from them after He had given him victory over them because of the remnants of the Muslims who had remained in them after He had given him victory over them, out of aversion to trampling on them without knowledge. And His statement, And God is All-Seeing of what you do, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And God is All-Seeing of your deeds and their deeds, and nothing of them is hidden from Him.
48:25: God the Almighty says: These polytheists from Quraysh are the ones who denied the Oneness of God, and prevented you, O believers in God, from entering the Sacred Mosque, and prevented the sacrificial animals from reaching their destination. The position of an is in the accusative case because it is connected, if you wish, to ma’kuf confined, or if you wish, to they prevented. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say in this regard: They prevented the sacrificial animals from reaching their destination. What God Almighty meant by His saying: that he reaches his place is that he reaches the place of his slaughter, which is entering the sanctuary, and the place where, when he reaches it, his slaughter is permissible. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had brought with him when he went out to Mecca on that journey of his, seventy camels. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Muslim Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah Ibn Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Al-Miswar Ibn Makhramah and Marwan Ibn Al-Hakam, that they told him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah intending to visit the House, not intending to fight. He brought with him seventy sacrificial animals, and the people were seven hundred men, so each sacrificial animal was for ten. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque and the offering, prevented from reaching its destination, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatada: They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from al-Masjid al-Haram while the sacrificial offerings were held back means, detained from reaching their destination. The Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions set out to perform Umrah in Dhul-Qa`dah, with the sacrificial offerings. When they reached al-Hudaybiyyah, the polytheists stopped them. The Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made peace with them on the condition that he would return that year and then the following year. He would stay in Makkah for three nights, and would not enter it except with the weapons of a rider, and that no one of its people would leave. So they slaughtered the sacrificial offerings, shaved their heads, and cut their hair. When it was the following year, the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions set out until they entered Makkah to perform Umrah in Dhul-Qa`dah. He stayed there for three nights. The polytheists had committed adultery with him when they turned him back, so God distanced him from them and brought him into Makkah in the same month in which they had turned him back. Then God revealed: A sacred month for a sacred month, and for sacred things there is equal retribution Al-Baqarah 2:149. Muhammad ibn ‘Amara al-Asadi and Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told me, and the wording is from Ibn ‘Amara. They said: ‘Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, saying: ‘Musa ibn ‘Ubaydah told us, on the authority of Iyas ibn Salamah ibn al-Akwa’, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn ‘Amr, Huwaytib ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza, and Hafs ibn so-and-so to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to make peace with him. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw them, including Suhayl ibn ‘Umar, he said: ‘God has made your affair easy for you. The people are coming to you because of their kinship ties and are asking you for peace, so send offerings and make the Talbiyah clear, perhaps that will soften their hearts.’ So they responded from the outskirts of the camp until their voices shook with the Talbiyah. They came and asked him for peace. While the people had made peace, and among the Muslims were some polytheists, Abu Sufyan was told about it. Then the valley was flowing with men. Iyas said, Salamah said: ‘So I came with six polytheists.’” Armed, I drove them, they did not possess for themselves benefit or harm, so I brought them to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he did not take any loot or kill them, and he pardoned them. He said: So we attacked those of us who were in the hands of the polytheists, and we did not leave a man of us in their hands except that we rescued him. He said: And we defeated those of them who were in our hands, then the Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn Amr and Huwaytaba, and they carried out their peace treaty, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali in his peace treaty, so Ali wrote between them: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, this is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with the Quraysh, he made peace with them on the condition that there would be no ihram or full moon, and that whoever of the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Mecca as a pilgrim or performer of the minor pilgrimage, or seeking God’s bounty, his blood and property would be safe, and whoever of the Quraysh came to Medina passing through to Egypt or Syria seeking God’s bounty, his blood and property would be safe, and whoever of the Quraysh came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be returned to them, and whoever Whoever comes to them from the companions of Muhammad, then it is theirs. This was very difficult for the Muslims, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever comes to them from us, may God distance him, and whoever comes to us from them, we will return him to them. God knows Islam in his soul and has made a way out for him.” So they made peace with him on the condition that he would perform Umrah the following year in this month, and that he would not enter upon us with horses or weapons, except what a traveler carries in his skins, and that he would stay with us for three nights, and that this sacrificial animal, wherever we detained it, would be placed in its place and he would not give it precedence over us. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: We will drive it and you turn back its destination. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out with the sacrificial animal and the people set out.” Muhammad ibn ‘Amara told me: ‘Ubayd God ibn Musa told us: Musa told us: Abu Marra, the freed slave of Umm Hani’, told me on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “The sacrificial animals were near the mountains overlooking Wadi al-Thaniyah. The polytheists approached them and turned them away. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered the sacrificial animals when they stopped them, which was al-Hudaybiyyah, and shaved his head. Some people took comfort in his vision when they saw him shave his head and others waited. They said: ‘Perhaps we will circumambulate the House.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘May God have mercy on those who shave their heads.’ It was said: ‘And those who cut their hair short.’ He...And those who cut their hair short.’” Ibn Humayd narrated: Al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated: Umar ibn Dhir al-Hamadani narrated on the authority of Mujahid: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Umrah three times, all of them in Dhul-Qa’dah. He returned to Madinah for each of them, including the Umrah in which he slaughtered the sacrificial animal, slaughtering it in its place, near the tree. They stipulated that he would come the following year to perform Umrah, enter Makkah, and circumambulate the House for three days, then leave. They would not prevent anyone who had come with him from leaving him, and he would not take out from Makkah anyone who had been there before his arrival from the Muslims. So, the following year, he entered Makkah and stayed there for three days, circumambulating the House. When the third day was close to noon, they sent to him: Your people have been annoyed by your stay. So, it was announced to the al-Nas 114:The sun will not set while there are any Muslims who have come with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out at the time of al-Hudaybiyyah with some ten hundred of his companions. When they were at Dhu al-Hulayfah, he garlanded the sacrificial animals and marked them, and entered ihram for ‘Umrah. He sent a spy of his from Khuza’ah ahead of him to inform him about Quraysh. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out until he was at Ghadir al-Ashtat, near Qaiqan. His spy from Khuza’ah came to him and said: ‘I have left Ka’b ibn Lu’ay and ‘Amir ibn Lu’ay, and they have gathered the Abyssinians against you and have gathered forces against you. They will fight you and prevent you from the House.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Advise me. Do you think that we should attack the descendants of those who helped them and give them a share? If they stay, they will stay resentful and sad, and if they give in, it will be a neck that God has severed. Or do you think that we should go to the House, and whoever prevents us from it, we will fight him?’ Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, God said: We did not come to fight anyone, but whoever comes between us and the House, we will fight him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Then go. Abu Hurairah used to say: I have never seen anyone who consulted his companions more than the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So they went until they were part of the way. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with the cavalry of the Quraysh in the vanguard, so take the right. By God, Khalid did not notice them until he was at the rear of the army. He set off running as a warning to the Quraysh. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went on until he was at the pass from which he would descend upon them. His mount knelt down. The people said: It has come, it has come. He said: What has come? They said, “Al-Qaswa’ has become empty.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, It has not become empty, and that is not its nature, but it was held back by the One who held back the elephant. Then he said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they will not ask me for a plan by which they can honor the sacred things of God except that I will give it to them. Then he was rebuked and leapt up, and turned away from them until he reached the furthest part of Al-Hudaybiyyah, near a small well of water. People only quench their thirst by drinking it. The people soon began to draw water from it. He complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of his thirst, so he took an arrow from his quiver and ordered them to put it in it. By God, he continued to bring them water until they left it. While they were like that, Badil ibn Warqa’ Al-Khuza’i came with a group of Khuza’ah, and they were the retinue of sincere advice from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people of Tihamah. He said, “I have left Ka’b ibn Lu’ay and ‘Amir ibn Lu’ay, and they have come down near the waters of Al-Hudaybiyyah, with them are the protection of the tribes. They are your fighters and they have prevented you from the House.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We did not come to fight anyone. But we came as pilgrims, and the Quraysh were exhausted and harmed by the war. If they wish, we will extend their time and let me be left alone with the people. If I prevail, then if they wish to do what the people have done, they will do so, otherwise they have stopped. But if they refuse, then by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will fight them over this matter of mine until my forelock is separated, or God carries out His command. Budayl said, We will inform them of what you say. So he set off until he came to the Quraysh and said, “We have come to you from this man, and we heard him say something. If you wish us to present it to you, we will.” Their fools said, We have no need for you to tell us anything about him. Those of them who possessed sound judgment said, Tell us what you heard him say. He said, I heard him say such and such. So he narrated to them what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had said. Then Urwah ibn Mas`ud ath-Thaqafi stood up and said, O people, are you not the son? They said, Yes. He said, Am I not the father? They said, Yes. He said, Do you accuse me? They said: No. He said: Do you not know that I mobilized the people of Ukaz, and when they insisted on me, I came to you with my family, my children and those who obeyed me? They said: Yes. He said: This man has offered you a plan of guidance, so accept it and let me go to him. They said: Go to him. So he went to him and began speaking to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said something similar to what he had said to Badil. At that, Urwah said: O Muhammad, tell me, if I exterminate your people, have you ever heard of anyone among the Arabs who had eradicated their roots before you? If it is the other way around, by God, I see faces and nobles among the people who would flee and leave you. Abu Bakr said: Suck the clitoris of Al-Lat - and Al-Lat was the tyrant of Thaqeef whom they worshipped - should we flee and leave him? He said: Who is this? They said: Abu Bakr. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, were it not for the favor you did me which I did not repay you for, I would have answered you. He started speaking to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and every time he spoke to him, he grabbed his beard. Al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba was standing over the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with a sword and a helmet. Every time Urwah reached for the Messenger of God’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) beard, he struck his hand with the blade of the sword and said: Take your hand away from his beard. He raised his head and said: Who is this? They said: Al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba. He said: What treachery? Did I not participate in your treachery? Al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba had accompanied some people during the pre-Islamic era, killed them and seized their wealth. Then he came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: As for Islam, we have accepted it, but as for the wealth, it is the wealth of treachery and we have no need of it. And Urwa kept gazing at the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with his eyes. By God, whenever the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who would rub it on his face and skin. When he gave them an order, they would rush to do what he ordered. When he performed ablution, they would almost fight over his ablution water. When he spoke, they would lower their voices in his presence, but they would not stare at him out of respect for him. Urwa returned to his companions and said: O people, by God, I have been a delegation to kings, and I have been a delegation to Caesar, Chosroes, and the Negus. By God, I have never seen a king whose companions respect him as much as the companions of Muhammad respect Muhammad. By God, whenever the Prophet spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who would rub it on his face and skin. When he gave them an order, they would rush to do what he ordered. When he performed ablution, they would almost fight over his ablution water. When they spoke in his presence, they would lower their voices, but they would not stare at him out of respect for him. He has offered you a plan of guidance, so accept it. A man from Kinanah said: Let me go to him. They said: Go to him. When he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who venerate sacrificial animals, so send them to him. So he sent them to him, and some people met him chanting the Talbiyah. When he saw that, he said: Glory be to God, it is not appropriate for these people to be prevented from the House. A man from among them called Mukraz ibn Hafs stood up and said: Let me go to him. They said: Go to him. When he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is Mukraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man. So he came and began to speak to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and while he was speaking to him, Suhayl ibn Amr came. Ayyub said: Ikrimah said: When Suhayl came, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Your matter has been made easy for you. Al-Zuhri said: Then Suhayl ibn Amr came and said: Come, let us write a document between us and you. So he called the scribe and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Write: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. So he said: What is the Most Gracious? By God, I do not know what it is, but write: In Your Name, O God, as you used to write. The Muslims said: By God, we will not write it except in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Write: In Your Name, O God. Then he said: Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed upon. Suhayl said: By God, if we knew that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have prevented you from the House, nor would we have fought you, but write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: By God, I am the Messenger of God, even if you call me a liar, but write Muhammad ibn Abdullah. Al-Zuhri said: That is because he said: By God, they will not ask me for a plan to glorify the sacred things of God except that I give it to them. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: On the condition that you leave us alone with the House so that we may circumambulate it. Suhayl said: By God, the Arabs will not say that we took a pressure, but you will have it from next year. So he wrote. Suhayl said: And on the condition that no man from us comes to you, even if we are of your religion, except that you return him to us. The Muslims said: Glory be to God, and how can he be returned to the polytheists when he came as a Muslim? While they were like that, Abu Jandal bin Suhayl bin Amr came, swaying in his chains, having come out from the lower part of Mecca and thrown himself down among the Muslims. Suhayl said, O Muhammad, this is the first person I will sue you for, that you return him to us. The Prophet said, Then grant him asylum to me. The Prophet said, I will not grant him asylum to you. The Prophet said, Yes, do so. The Prophet said, I will not. His companion, Mukraz, with Suhayl beside him, said, We have granted him asylum to you. Abu Jandal said, O group of Muslims, shall I be returned to the polytheists when I came as a Muslim? Don’t you see what I have suffered? He had been severely tortured for the sake of God. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: By God, I never doubted since I embraced Islam except on that day. I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Are we not upon the truth and our enemy is upon falsehood? He said: Yes. I said: Then why would we give up our religion? He said: I am the Messenger of God, and I will not disobey Him, and He will support me. I said: Didn’t you tell us that we will come to the House and perform Tawaf around it? He said: Yes. I said: Did I tell you that you will come to it this year? I said: No. He said: Then I will come to it and perform Tawaf around it. I said: Then I came to Abu Bakr and said: Is this not truly the Prophet of God? He said: Yes. I said: Are we not upon the truth and our enemy is upon falsehood? He said: Yes. I said: Then why would we give up our religion? He said: O man, he is the Messenger of God, and he does not disobey his Lord, so hold fast to his roots until you die, for by God, he is upon the truth. I said: Didn’t he tell us that we will come to the House and perform Tawaf around it? He said: Yes. Did he tell you that you will come to it this year? He said: No. He said: Then you will come to it and circumambulate it. Az-Zuhri said: Umar said: So I did some work for that. When he finished his story, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his companions: Get up and slaughter, then shave your head. He said: By God, not a single one of us got up until he had said that three times. When none of them got up, he got up and went to Umm Salamah and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah said: O Messenger of God, do you like that? He said: Go out, and do not say a word to any of them until you slaughter your sacrifice and call your barber to shave you. So he got up and went out and did not say a word to any of them until he slaughtered his sacrifice and called his barber to shave him. When they saw that, they got up and slaughtered, and some of them shaved each other until some of them almost killed each other out of grief. Then believing women came to him, and God, the Exalted, the Majestic, revealed to him: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants until he reached by protecting the disbelieving women. He said: So on that day, Umar divorced two of his wives who were polytheists. He said: So he forbade them from returning them, and ordered them to return the dowry at that time. A man said to Al-Zuhri: Is it for the sake of the private parts? He said: Yes, so one of them married Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other married Safwan ibn Umayyah. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to Medina, and Abu Basir, a man from the Quraysh who was a Muslim, came to him. He sent two men after him, and they said: The covenant that you made for us. So he gave it to the two men, and they went out with it until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, and they stopped to eat some of their dates. Abu Basir said to one of the two men: By God, I see that this sword of yours, so-and-so, is good. So the other drew it and said: By God, it is good. I have tried it and tried it. Abu Basir said: Show me, so I can see it! So he got hold of him and beat him with it until he cooled down. The other ran until he reached Madinah and entered the mosque running. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This one saw panic and said: By God, my companion was killed. By God, I am going to be killed. Then Abu Basir came and said: By God, you have fulfilled your promise and you have returned me to them. Then God helped me against them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to his mother, a war-monger if he had anyone. When he heard this, he knew that he would return him to them. He said: So he went out until he reached Saif al-Bahr, and Abu Jandal ibn Sahil ibn Umar escaped and joined Abu Basir. No man from Quraysh who had converted to Islam would leave without joining Abu Basir until a group of them gathered. By God, they would not hear of a camel going out to Quraysh to Syria except that they would intercept them and kill them and take their money. Quraysh sent to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, imploring him by God and kinship to send to them. Whoever comes to him is safe. Then God revealed: And it is He who has restrained their hands from you and your hands from them until he reached the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance and their fanaticism was They did not acknowledge that he was a prophet, nor did they acknowledge In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and they stood between them and the House. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa`id narrated to us: `Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: Mu`ammar informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of `Urwah, on the authority of al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out at the time of al-Hudaybiyyah with some ten hundred men.” Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said in his hadith: al-Zuhri said: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated to me that `Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: “So I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘Are you not the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He also said: Abu Nusayr and those who had converted to Islam from those whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had sent back went out until they reached the coast on the roads of the Quraysh caravan, and they killed the infidels who were on it and seized it as booty. When the infidels of Quraysh saw that, a group of them rode to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said to him: ‘Your period will be of no avail, while we are being killed and our wealth is being plundered. We ask you to include these people among those who have converted to Islam in your peace treaty and to protect them.’” And he prevented us from fighting him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that, and God revealed: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them. Then he led the hadith to its end, similar to the hadith of Ibn Abd al-A’la. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that they both narrated to him, saying: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, intending to visit the House, not intending to fight. He brought with him his offering of seventy camels, until when he was in Usfan, Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Ka’bi met him and said to him: ‘O Messenger of God, these are the Quraysh who have heard of your march.’ So they set out with them, wearing tiger skins, and they camped at Dhu Tuwa, making a covenant with God that you would never enter it upon them. And here is Khalid ibn al-Walid with their cavalry, which they have advanced to Kara’ al-Ghamim. He said: ‘So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Woe to the Quraysh! War has destroyed them. What would they suffer if they left me alone with the rest of the Arabs? If they defeat me, that will be what they wanted, and if God gives me victory over them, they will enter Islam in humiliation.’ Then he mentioned something like the hadith of Muammar with many additions to the hadith of Muammar that I have omitted to mention.”. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And the sacrificial offerings are to be held back until they reach their destination, he said: “The sacrificial offerings were at Dhu Tuwa, and Al-Hudaybiyah was outside the sanctuary. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped there when the water sank for him from the Quraysh.” And His statement, And had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, lest you trample them and there befall you on their part a disgrace without your knowledge, God Almighty says: And had it not been for believing men and believing women among them, O believers in God, lest you trample them with your cavalry and infantry, you would not have known them in Mecca, and the polytheists have kept them from you there, so that because of that they cannot come out to you so that you may kill them. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And had it not been for believing men and believing women, until he reached without knowledge, this was when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were not allowed to enter Mecca, and there were believing men and believing women in it, so God hated that they should harm or trample without knowledge, so that a disgrace should befall you from them without knowledge. The people of interpretation differed regarding the shame that God meant in this place. Some of them said: He meant sin. Who said that? Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, lest you trample them and there should befall you on their part a sin without knowledge, he said: A sin without knowledge. Others said: He meant the blood money. Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And a disgrace befalls you on their part without your knowledge, so you pay the blood money, but as for the sin, he did not hold it against them. Disgrace is the verbal noun from ‘arr, which is scabies. The meaning is: And a disgrace befalls you on their part that makes you look sick, for which you must pay the expiation for accidental killing, which is freeing a believing slave, for whoever is able to do that, and for whoever is not able to do that, then he must fast for two months. Rather, I chose this statement rather than the one said by Ibn Ishaq because God only made it obligatory for the killer of a believer in the land of war, if he had not emigrated from it and his killer was not aware of his faith, to pay expiation rather than blood money. He said: And if he is from a people enemy to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave He did not make it obligatory for his killer to pay blood money by mistake. Therefore, we said: What is meant by disgrace in this place is expiation, and that what He said: that you trample them is in the nominative case in response to the men, because the meaning of the statement is: And were it not that you trample believing men and believing women without knowing it, and a disgrace befalls you from them without your knowledge, God would have permitted you, O believers, to enter Mecca. But He prevented you from that. That God may admit into His mercy whom He wills means: That God may admit into Islam from the people of Mecca whomever He wills before you enter it. The answer to had it not been was omitted because the statement indicated it. And His statement, If they had separated, means: If those among the polytheists of Mecca, the believing men and believing women, whom you did not know, had separated from them and left them, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment, meaning: We would have killed whoever remained in it with the sword, or We would have destroyed them with some of what would cause them pain from Our immediate punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, If you were to separate… the verse indicates that God protects the believers from the disbelievers. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, If only they had moved away, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them, meaning the people of Mecca, among whom were weak believers. God says, Had it not been for those weak ones, if they had moved away, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment. Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, If they were to separate, if they were to separate, and the believer were to separate from the disbeliever, then We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.:
48:26: God Almighty means by His saying: When those who disbelieved put into their hearts the fanaticism of the times of ignorance when Suhayl ibn Amr put the fanaticism into his heart, so he refused to write in the book of litigation that was before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and to write in it: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and he and his people refused to enter the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that year. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: Their fanaticism, which God mentioned, when those who disbelieved had placed fanaticism in their hearts, was the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance, that they did not recite In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful and they stood between themselves and the House. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Yahya bin Saeed told us: Abdullah bin Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, something similar. Amr ibn Muhammad al-Uthmani told me: Ismail ibn Abi Uways told us: My brother told me, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God,’ then his wealth and his life are protected from me, except for what is due to him, and his reckoning is with God. And God revealed in His Book, and mentioned a people who were arrogant, saying, ‘Indeed, when it was said to them, “There is no god but God,” they were arrogant.’ And God said, ‘When those who disbelieved put into their hearts conceit - the conceit of ignorance - then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and made the word of righteousness binding upon them. And they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it.’ And it is, ‘There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God.’ The polytheists were arrogant about it on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, the day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them regarding the period of time.” And when from his saying, When those who disbelieved made from the connection of his saying: We would have punished... and the interpretation of the statement: We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment, when those who disbelieved made fanaticism in their hearts, and fanaticism is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so protected his nose with fanaticism and a protection, and from it is the saying of Al-Mutalammiss: But I am one of them and my honor is their honor. Thus the head protects its nose from being pinched. What he means by his saying: protects is: prevents. And he said, the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance, because what they did was all the behavior of the people of disbelief, and none of it was something that God had given them permission to do, nor any of His messengers. And His statement, So God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, meaning, the Most High says, “So God sent down patience, reassurance, and dignity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, when those who disbelieved were protected with the zeal of the Age of Ignorance, and prevented them from circumambulating the House, and refused to write in the book between them, ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God.’ And He made them adhere to the word of piety,” meaning He made them adhere to the statement, There is no god but God, by which they would protect themselves from the Fire and the painful torment. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, with differences among them, and the report was narrated about it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Those who said that mentioned what we said about it, and the report that we mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah Al-Bahili told us: Sufyan bin Habib told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Thawr bin Abi Fakhitah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Tufayl, on the authority of his father, who heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: And make them adhere to the word of piety. He said: There is no god but God. Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash Al-Ataki told me: I heard Salim, he heard Shu’bah, he heard Salamah bin Kuhayl, he heard Ubayya, he heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement, And bind them to the word of piety, he said: There is no god but God. Ibn Bashar told me: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ubayya ibn Rib’i, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement, And bind them to the word of piety, he said: There is no god but God, and God is greatest. Muhammad ibn Isa al-Damaghani told me: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Shu’bah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: There is no god but God, and God is the greatest. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Wahb bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ubayyah, on the authority of a man from Banu Tamim, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: And make them adhere to the word of piety. He said: There is no god but God. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And bind them to the word of piety, meaning the testimony that there is no god but God, so it is a word of piety. He says: It is the head of piety. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: I heard Abu Ishaq narrating on the authority of Amr Ibn Maymun that he used to say regarding this verse, And He bound them to the word of piety, he said: There is no god but God. Muhammad bin Isa told me: Ibn al-Mubarak told us: Sufyan told me on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, similarly. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun: And make them adhere to the word of piety. He said: There is no god but God. He said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: And he made them adhere to the word of piety. He said: There is no god but God. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And make them adhere to the word of piety, which is: the testimony that there is no god but God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And bind them to the word of piety, that it is There is no god but God. Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Hafs bin Omar told us: Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement, And bind them to the word of piety, he said: The testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn Al-Barqi told me: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani: And he made them adhere to the word of piety. He said: There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Al-Sawari Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Suwar narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Khalid al-Makki, on the authority of Ali al-Azdi, who said: “I was with Ibn Umar between Mecca and Mina at the two crossings, and he heard the people saying: ‘There is no god but God, and God is the Greatest.’ He said: ‘It is it.’ I said: ‘What is it?’ He said: ‘And he made them adhere to the word of piety - sincerity - and they were the most deserving of it and the most worthy of it.’” Others said: Rather, it is the word of piety and sincerity. Who said that? Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Azdi told me: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And make them adhere to the word of piety. He said: Sincerity. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The word of piety means the word of sincerity. Others said: It is his saying: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Who said that? Muhammad bin Isa told me: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding his statement, And he bound them to the word of piety, he said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Others said: It is: There is no god but God alone, He has no partner, His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. Those who said that: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us: Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’: And he made them adhere to the word of piety. One of them said: Sincerity, and the other said: The word of piety is: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent. And His statement, And they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it, God Almighty says: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers were the people of the word of piety, not the polytheists. It was mentioned that it was in the reading of Abdullah and they were its people and most deserving of it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And they were more deserving of it and its people. The Muslims were more deserving of it and they were its al-Nas 114:meaning monotheism, and the testimony that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. And His statement, And God is All-Knowing of all things, God Almighty says: And God has always been All-Knowing of all things, nothing that will happen is hidden from Him. And because of His knowledge, O people, of what will happen when you enter Mecca, and in it are believing men and believing women whom you do not know, He has not permitted you to enter Mecca on this journey of yours.
48:27: God Almighty says: God has fulfilled for His Messenger Muhammad the vision that He showed him, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred House of God in safety, not fearing the polytheists, some of them cutting their hair short, and some of them shaving their heads. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, in safety.” He said: It is the entry of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers into the House, with their heads shaved and their hair cut short. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, on the authority of Abu Asim, who said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, who said: Al-Hasan told us, who said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The vision is true, he said: I saw at Al-Hudaibiyah that he would enter Mecca with his companions shaved. His companions said when he slaughtered at Al-Hudaibiyah: Where is the vision of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that he was circumambulating the House with his companions, and God fulfilled his vision, and said: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, in safety... until he reached you will not fear. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger, he said: I saw in a dream that they were entering the Sacred Mosque, and that they were safe, with their heads shaved and their hair cut short. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about the statement, God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger… the verse, he said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them, ‘Indeed, I have seen that you will enter Paradise with your heads shaved and your hair cut short.’ But when the battle of Hudaybiyyah was completed and he had not entered that year, the hypocrites disputed that and said, ‘Where was his vision?’ God said, ‘Indeed, God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger.’ Then he recited until he reached, ‘and with your hair cut short, having no fear.’ I see that he will enter it this year, and that will happen.” Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger... until His saying, God willing, in safety, regarding the vision of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which he saw that he would enter Mecca in safety, not afraid. He said: Shaving and cutting your hair, not afraid. And His statement, Then He knew what you did not know, means, the Most High, the Majestic, the Most Glorious, that God, the Most High, knew what you did not know. That is His knowledge, the Most High, of the believing men and women in Mecca, whom the believers did not know about. Had they entered it that year, He would have trampled them on with horses and foot, and they would have suffered a disgrace from them without their knowledge. So God turned them back from Mecca because of that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Then He knew what you did not know, that He returned him to a place among them among the believing men and women, and delayed him so that God would include in His mercy whomever He wills whom He wants to guide. And His saying, And He made for them a near victory. The people of interpretation differed regarding the near victory that God made for the believers before they entered the Sacred Mosque with their heads shaved and their hair cut short. Some of them said: It is the peace treaty that took place between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists of Quraysh. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, A victory soon to come, he said: The sacrifice at Al-Hudaibiyah, and they returned and conquered Khaybar. Then he performed Umrah after that, and his vision was confirmed the following year. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, regarding his statement, And He made a near conquest before that, meaning the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. And no conquest in Islam was greater than that. Fighting took place where people met, but when the truce came, war was stopped, and all people felt safe with one another. So they met and negotiated, discussed, and disputed. No one spoke about Islam with any understanding except that he entered into it. So in those two years, as many as had been in Islam before that, or more. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Then He made a near victory before that. He said: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Others said: What is meant by the imminent conquest in this place is the conquest of Khaybar. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And He granted a near conquest before that, that Khaybar was conquered by God when they returned from Hudaybiyyah, and He divided it among all the people of Hudaybiyyah except for one man from the Ansar, called Abu Dujana Samak ibn Kharsha, who had witnessed Hudaybiyyah but was absent from Khaybar. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God informed us that He granted His Messenger and those who were with him from the people of the Pledge of Ridwan a near victory without their entering the Sacred Mosque and without his believing the vision of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the conquest of Khaybar were before that, and God, the Most High, did not specify His report of that victory over that victory, rather He included that, and all of that was a victory that God granted without that. The correct view is that it includes him as he did, so it is said: God made the vision of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of him and his companions entering the Sacred Mosque with their heads shaved and their hair cut short, not fearing the polytheists, the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the conquest of Khaybar, as proof of his belief.
48:28: He, the Most High, means by His statement, It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with clear proof and the religion of truth, which is Islam, which He sent calling His creation to it, to make it prevail over all religions, meaning: to invalidate all religions with it, until there is no religion other than it. And that will be the case until Jesus, son of Mary, descends and kills the Antichrist, at which point all religions will be invalidated, except the religion of God that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, preached, and Islam will prevail over all religions. And His saying, And sufficient is God as a witness, means that God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, I call you, O Muhammad, to witness that your Lord will make manifest the religion with which He sent you. “And sufficient is God as a witness,” meaning that He is sufficient for you as a witness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Yahya ibn Wadh narrated: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated from al-Hasan: “It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions. And sufficient is God as Witness.” He said: I bear witness for you regarding Himself that He will make your religion prevail over all religions. This was an announcement from God, the Most High, to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and to those of his companions who hated the treaty on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, that God had opened for them Mecca and other lands, thus comforting them from the depression and grief that had befallen them, as a result of their leaving Mecca before entering it and before performing the circumambulation of the House.
48:29: And His statement, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves, God Almighty says: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and his followers from among his companions who are with him in his religion, are harsh against the disbelievers, their hearts are harsh toward them, and their mercy toward them is little. Merciful among themselves, He says: Their hearts are tender toward one another, their souls are gentle toward them, and they are easy on them. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Merciful among themselves means God has put mercy into their hearts, some to others. You see them bowing and prostrating means: You see them bowing sometimes to God in their prayers and sometimes prostrating. Seeking bounty from God means: They seek, through their bowing and prostration and their severity against the disbelievers and their mercy to one another, bounty from God, and that is His mercy to them, by His favoring them and admitting them into His Paradise. And approval means: And that their Lord be pleased with them. His saying, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, means: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration during their prayer. Then the people of interpretation differed about the mark that God meant in this place. Some of them said: That is a mark that God places on the faces of the believers on the Day of Resurrection, by which they will be known for their prostration to Him in this world. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: Their prayers will be evident on their faces on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaidullah Al-Atki told us on the authority of Khalid Al-Hanafi, regarding his statement, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: This will be known on the Day of Resurrection in their faces from the traces of their prostration in this world, and it is like His statement, You will recognize in their faces the radiance of pleasure. al-Mutaffifin 83:24 Ubaid bin Asbat bin Muhammad told me: My father told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah, regarding his statement: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, he said: The places of prostration on their faces on the Day of Resurrection will be whiter. Muhammad bin Amara told us: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Atiyyah, something similar. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Atiyah, something similar. Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Fadil told us on the authority of Atiyah, something similar. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us: I heard Shabib say on the authority of Muqatil from Hayyan: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: The light on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Harun bin Ismail told us: Ali bin Al-Mubarak said: I heard more than one person on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, he said: Whiteness on their faces on the Day of Resurrection. Others said: Rather, this is a characteristic of Islam, its mark and piety, and what he meant by that is that he sees that from them in this world. Who said that? Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Their mark is on their faces, he said: Good looks. He said: Mujahid told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Hasan bin Amara told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, he said: It is not what you see, but it is the mark of Islam, its complexion, its countenance, and its humility. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amer told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: Humility and humility. Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. He said: Abu Amer told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: Humility. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding this verse, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, he said: The complexion. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, he said: It is humility. I said: Is it the trace of prostration? He said: It will be between his eyes like the knee of a goat, and it is as God wills. Others said: This is a mark that appears on the faces of those who pray, like the mark of staying up late, which appears on the face, such as melasma, irritation, yellowness, and the like, which is shown by staying up late and fatigue on the face. They interpreted this as a sign in this world. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: The yellowness. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us on the authority of his father, who said: The sheikh who used to recite verses in difficulty claimed that he recited Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, and he claimed that staying up late could be seen on their faces. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah, regarding his statement, Their mark is on their faces, he said: It is irritation on the face from staying up all night. Others said: These are traces that are seen on the face from the dust of the earth, or the dew of purification. Who said that? Hawthara bin Muhammad Al-Manqari told us: Hammad bin Mas’adah told us, and Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us both on the authority of Tha’laba bin Suhayl, on the authority of Ja’far bin Ibn Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, regarding his statement, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, he said: The dust of the earth and the dew of purification. Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Harun bin Ismail told us: Ali bin Al-Mubarak told us: Malik bin Dinar told us: I heard Ikrimah say, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: It is the trace of the dust. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God, the Exalted, has informed us that the mark of these people, whose features He described on their faces, is from the effect of prostration, and He did not specify a specific time over another. Since this is the case, then it applies to all times. Thus, their mark by which they were known in this world was the effect of Islam, and that is its humility, guidance, asceticism, and characteristic, and the effects of performing its obligatory and voluntary acts. And in the Hereafter, He has informed us that they will be known by it, and that is the radiance in the face, and the whiteness of the hands and feet from the effect of ablution, and the whiteness of the faces from the effect of prostration. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of the mark, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: Their sign is that I have taught them the prayer. His saying, That is their description in the Torah, means: This description that I have described to you is of the description of the followers of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who are with him, and their description is in the Torah. And His statement, And their example in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its shoot, meaning: Their description in the Gospel of Jesus is like a seed which sends forth its shoot, which is its young ones. It is said from this: the seed has sprung forth, meaning it has sprouted, so it sprouts, and they are likened to the sprout-grown seed because they began to enter Islam, and they were a small number, then they began to increase, and a group entered it after them, then a group after a group, until their number increased, as happens with the origin of the seed, from which the young ones arise after it until it increases and grows. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Muhammad is the Messenger of God and those with him: his companions are like them, meaning their description written in the Torah and the Gospel before the heavens and the earth were created. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid told us on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are hard against the disbelievers…until His saying: That is their example in the Torah. Then he said: And their example in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its shoot…the verse. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Their example in the Torah means this example in the Torah: And their example in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its shoot. This is the example of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Gospel. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, he said, “That is their example in the Torah and their example in the Gospel: like a seed which sends forth its shoot.” It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, “Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah,” meaning the mark on their faces is like their description in the Torah, but not like their description in the Gospel. Then the Almighty said, And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its shoot... the verse. This is their description in the Gospel. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, “Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah and their description in the Gospel: like a seed which sends forth its shoot.” Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding the statement of God: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him... the verse. He said: This is their example in the Torah and another example in the Gospel: Like a seed which sends forth its shoot and makes it strong the verse. Others said: These two examples in the Torah and the Bible are like them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hussein told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, That is their example in the Torah, and the Gospel are one. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of those who said: Their example in the Torah is not their example in the Gospel. The report of their example in the Torah ends at His statement: That is their example in the Torah. This is because if the statement were as Mujtahid said, that their example in the Torah and the Gospel are the same, then the revelation would have been: And their example in the Gospel is like a seed that sends forth its shoots. So their example of the seed would have been connected to His statement: Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration, so that would be a report of that being their example in the Torah and the Gospel. The fact that the statement comes without the waw in His statement: like a seed is clear evidence of the correctness of what we said, and that their statement: And their example in the Gospel is a report of their description that is in the Gospel and not what is in the Torah of it. And in a manner similar to what we said about His statement, He brought forth its branch, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah, who said: While Abdullah was teaching a man to recite at sunset, he passed by this verse: Like a seed which sends forth its stalk. He said: You are the seed, and your harvest is near. He said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Hamid al-Tawil, who said: Anas bin Malik recited: Like a seed which sends forth its shoot and makes it strong. He said: Do you know what its shoot is? He said: Its plants. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, “That is their example in the Torah and their example in the Gospel: like a seed which sends forth its stalk,” he said: Its ear when its plant emerges from its grains. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Their example in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its stalk. He said: This is the example of the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Gospel. It was said to them: “A people will emerge who will produce the plants of a seed. Among them will be a people who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and al-Zuhri: Like a plant that sends forth its shoots. They said: It sends forth its plants. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And their example in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its shoot, meaning: The companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be few, then they will increase and multiply and become coarse. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, Like a seed that sends forth its shoot, his children, then his children increased. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Like a seed that sends forth its shoot, he said: What grows beside the field and matures and grows. His saying, So he supported it, means: he strengthened it, meaning he strengthened the plant’s roots and helped it. This is from mu’azaara, which means assistance. Fastaghlaza, means: the plant became thick. So it stood firm on its stalk. The stalk is the plural of stalk, and the stalk of the plant and the tree is its carrier. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: And strengthened it. He said: Its growth while it is wrapped up when the ear of corn is in the ears. That is their description in the Torah and their description in the Gospel.
