This is a description He made for the People of the Book: When a people emerge, they will sprout like a seed, and there will be men among them who will enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, then they will become harsh. They are the ones who were with them. This is a description He made for Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: God sent the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning: God sent the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on his own, then a few people gathered around him who believed in him, then the few will become many, and they will become harsh, and God will enrage the disbelievers for them. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So he supported him, he said: So he strengthened him and aided him. And his saying, On its market, he said: its roots. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and al-Zuhri: So He strengthened him, and he became thick and stood firm on his legs. He said: So they caught up with each other. Yunus urged me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Then he supported him, that this came together and was intertwined. He said: And so the believers went out, and they were few and weak. God never ceases to increase them and support them with Islam, just as He supported this plant with its children, so He supported it, and it was an example for the believers. Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid told me: Marwan ibn Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: Like a seed that sends forth its shoot, then makes it strong, then it becomes thick and stands firmly on its stalk. He said: A grain of wheat is scattered, and each grain sprouts as a single seed, then each one of them grows until it becomes thick and stands firmly on its stalk. He said: He said: The companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were few, then they became many, then they became thick so that God may enrage the disbelievers through them. And His statement, It amazes the farmers, that He may enrage the disbelievers thereby, says the Most High: This crop, which has grown thick and stood on its stalk in its perfection and good growth, and has reached maturity and reached maturity, amazes those who planted it. That He may enrage the disbelievers thereby. He says: So the example of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and their gathering together until they multiplied and grew, and their matter became thick, is like this crop whose description the Most High described. Then He said, That He may enrage the disbelievers thereby, so that indicates an omitted statement, which is that God, the Most High, did that with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, to enrage the disbelievers thereby. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: That He may enrage the disbelievers with them. God says: Their example is like that of a seed which sends forth its shoot and makes it strong, so it becomes thick and stands firmly on its stem until it reaches the best of plants. The farmers are amazed at its abundance and the beauty of its growth. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, It delights the farmers, that its beauty delights the farmers, so that He may enrage the disbelievers with them with the believers, because of their large number. This is their example in the Gospel. And His statement, God has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward, God Almighty says: God has promised those who believe in God and His Messenger, and do righteous deeds, meaning: and do what God has commanded them to do of His obligations that He has made obligatory upon them. His saying, from them means: from the shore that the crop brought forth, and they are those who entered Islam after the crop whose description our Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, described. The ha’ and the mim in His saying, from them refer to the meaning of the shore, not to its wording, and that is why it was made plural and was said from them, not from them. The shore was made plural because what was meant by it was those who entered the religion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Day of Resurrection after the group whose description God described in His saying, “And those with him are harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating.” His saying, and forgiveness, means: pardon for their past sins and bad deeds, and replace them with good ones. His saying, and a great reward, means: a generous recompense, and that is Paradise.
